holidays.name: 420 Day (4/20)
holidays.description: A cannabis-culture celebration observed worldwide every April 20, with gatherings, festivals, and mass meetups, most famously at 4:20 PM. Fans of the date also love how it lines up with the clock.
holidays.origin: Popularly traced to a group of San Rafael High School students in 1971 who called themselves the 'Waldos' and met at 4:20 PM to search for an abandoned cannabis crop. The term spread through the Grateful Dead community and later into mainstream culture.
holidays.funFact: Highway departments in Colorado and Idaho reportedly had to replace 420-mile-marker signs because fans kept stealing them, and Colorado eventually switched to 419.99.

holidays.name: National Pineapple Upside-Down Cake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the retro dessert with caramelized pineapple rings and maraschino cherries baked in a buttery brown sugar topping, then flipped to reveal the glossy fruit design.
holidays.origin: Upside-down cakes date back centuries, originally baked in cast-iron skillets over open fires. The pineapple version took off in 1925 after the Dole company ran a pineapple recipe contest and received thousands of entries for it.
holidays.funFact: Early upside-down cakes were made in skillets, which is why many classic recipes still call for cast iron.

holidays.name: National Cheddar Fries Day
holidays.description: A day for loaded, cheesy fries smothered in melted cheddar. Everyone is encouraged to enjoy a basket of fries and gooey cheddar sauce guilt-free.
holidays.origin: Like many modern food holidays, it appears to be an informal observance that grew from restaurant promotions and social media enthusiasm for cheese-topped fries rather than from any official proclamation.
holidays.funFact: Cheddar gets its name from the English village of Cheddar in Somerset, where the cheese was traditionally aged in nearby caves.

holidays.name: Chinese Language Day
holidays.description: A United Nations observance celebrating the history and culture of the Chinese language and promoting multilingualism, with calligraphy demonstrations, poetry readings, and language lessons.
holidays.origin: The UN established its language days in 2010 to celebrate multilingualism. Chinese Language Day is held on April 20 to honor Cangjie, the legendary inventor of Chinese characters, and coincides with Guyu, the 'Grain Rain' solar term.
holidays.funFact: According to legend, Cangjie had four eyes, and the heavens rained millet when characters were invented.

holidays.name: Lima Bean Respect Day
holidays.description: A humorous day dedicated to giving the often-maligned lima bean the respect it deserves, encouraging picky eaters to give the buttery legume a second chance.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food observance in the tradition of tongue-in-cheek bean-related days, created by food enthusiasts to rehabilitate the lima bean's reputation as a childhood dinner-table villain.
holidays.funFact: Lima beans are named after Lima, Peru, and have been cultivated in the Americas for thousands of years.
